drills.q: Greenfield analytics on Azure 2026: Fabric, Synapse, or Databricks? Decision tree.
drills.a: Default Fabric for MS-aligned BI+lakehouse (CU billing, OneLake, Power BI native). Databricks for ML lifecycle depth/Spark scale/multi-cloud/Unity Catalog. Synapse only for existing estates - new dedicated pools deprecated-by-guidance.

drills.q: Nightly Spark job slows month-end dashboards in Fabric. Root cause and fix?
drills.a: Shared CU pool: smoothed background usage raised baseline pressure; interactive requests delay first under throttling. Fix = capacity separation per workload severity/environment plus schedule staggering, not job tuning alone.

drills.q: Clickstream 200k events/s at ~500 bytes with strict per-user ordering. Design Event Hubs.
drills.a: ~100 MB/s -> Premium (~10-14 PUs) territory beyond Standard's ~40 MB/s ceiling. 64-128 partitions sized for parallelism headroom; partition key user_id for co-partitioned ordering; consumers <= partition count.

drills.q: Event Hubs consumers idle while lag grows. Why?
drills.a: More consumer instances than partitions - partitions cap consumer-group parallelism and extra instances sit idle. Raise partitions (Premium/Dedicated only) or repartition upstream; size instances to partition count.

drills.q: Serverless SQL exploration queries are blowing the budget. Controls?
drills.a: Partition files by date/predicate paths enabling pruning, enforce predicate pushdown patterns, isolate exploration into separate accounts with alerts, move production consumption to provisioned engines entirely.

drills.q: ADF copy from on-prem SQL Server - which IR and how run reliably?
drills.a: Self-hosted IR mandatory for private/on-prem sources: 2+ nodes sharing one IR for HA, sized VMs near data, patch policy defined, queue depth + heartbeats monitored.

drills.q: Synapse dedicated pool fine weekdays, regresses every Monday. Diagnosis order?
drills.a: Weekend-growth hash skew (uneven space usage/data movement in plans) -> stale statistics post-load -> tempdb contention from concurrent CTAS -> stale materialized views -> resource-class slot starvation via workload classifiers.

drills.q: OLTP changes must appear in dashboards within ~2 minutes. Two architectures?
drills.a: Fabric mirroring (Azure SQL/Cosmos -> OneLake Delta, Direct Lake dashboards, minimal code) or CDC -> Event Hubs -> eventstream/KQL for en-route transforms and sub-minute SLAs; never point BI at OLTP primaries directly.

drills.q: Same Spark logic: 40 min in Fabric notebook vs 8 min in Databricks. Plausible causes?
drills.a: Runtime version pinning, Native Execution Engine availability, pool sizing/node counts, V-order write overhead (~15-33% write-heavy stages), missing acceleration on specific operators, shortcut-vs-local data latency. If ML-lifecycle-heavy: keep on Databricks landing shared Delta.

drills.q: Rank incident frequency: CU throttling, partition starvation, scan-cost blowouts, pool skew regressions.
drills.a: 1 scan-cost blowouts (every per-scan model punishes exploration silently), 2 CU throttling (rises as Fabric concentrates workloads), 3 partition starvation (well-known, bites migrations), 4 pool skew (frozen legacy estates). Frequency tracks platform share x failure silence.

drills.q: Explain why cluster-billed warehouses and scan-billed query-in-place systems represent fundamentally different cost-modeling disciplines.
drills.a: Cluster-billed (Dedicated Pool, Redshift) requires capacity planning ahead of load; cost is roughly fixed whether the cluster is idle or fully loaded. Scan-billed (Serverless SQL Pool, BigQuery) shifts the discipline to controlling how much data each query scans -- partitioning and query design directly reduce cost, with no idle-capacity waste but real risk of cost surprise from an unexpectedly expensive ad-hoc query. Neither is universally cheaper; it depends on usage pattern.
